cohort: Newborns delivered in public hospitals of Mekelle City from February 21, 2020, to June 20, 2020, comprising 92 cases (macrosomic babies) and 184 controls (non-macrosomic babies) were included in the study.
finding: The study found that older maternal age, greater weight gain during pregnancy, higher maternal BMI, male sex of the newborn, and a maternal history of macrosomia were significantly associated with an increased risk of macrosomia.
